description:
visit_protocol_callback (src/compiler2/jobs/keying.rs ~648) sets every non-receiver argument's local result to Whole, so a callback is keyed on literal arguments. Measured: Enum.member?(kinds, :boolean) and its siblings give Enum.member?/2 nine keys, one per needle; List.member? called directly gives one. fz-afu.11 (closed) settled the dispatch half. After the accumulator and ownership fixes, one OptionParser.parse call still costs 214 keys and 2570 jobs against 251 jobs for an empty program; this is the largest remaining piece.

Needs its own proposal page (paper first: shrunk program, predicted keys) before any build. Related measured fan-out, same page: a pinned pattern and a guard operand are demanded Whole (keying.rs ~966); Keyword.get/3 keys per returned literal value (10-12 keys), the stated returned-axis rule working as written.

Proposal page: /Users/j5n/Workspace/optionparser-compile-cost.html (https://claude.ai/artifact/9MdFVrMJRKJcSULMazQfyo). Spike evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad.
title: A protocol callback's non-receiver arguments are keyed only where an implementation returns them
